    Contour functions induced by path realizations #

    For a reversed linear realization of a quiver, declare two parallel paths related when their values are nonzero scalar multiples. The unique scalar relating every such pair is a genuine contour function. Consequently Roiter-style contour-cohomology vanishing applies directly to the scalar discrepancies of a path realization.

    source
    def LargeIndecomposable.LinearPathCategory.nonzeroScalarMultiplePathRelation {k : Type u} [Field k] {Q : Type v} [Quiver Q] {D : Type z} [CategoryTheory.Category.{u_1, z} D] [CategoryTheory.Preadditive D] [CategoryTheory.Linear k D] (F₀ : Q → D) (F₁ : {i j : Q} → (i ⟶ j) → (F₀ j ⟶ F₀ i)) :
    PathContourRelation Q

    Two parallel paths are related when the first has nonzero realization and is a nonzero scalar multiple of the second. The second realization is then automatically nonzero as well.
